blocks.text: Setting up Google Sheets for media buyers on Mac

Google Sheets runs in your browser, but you can make it feel like a native Mac app. Open Chrome, go to sheets.google.com, and click the three-dot menu. Select Cast, Save, and Share, then click Install page as app. This creates a shortcut in your Applications folder. You can now pin it to your Dock and switch to it with ⌘ + Tab.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for your daily workflow

Speed is your best friend when managing large campaign datasets. Press ⌘ + / to see the full list of shortcuts inside Sheets. For quick navigation, use ⌘ + Arrow Keys to jump to the edge of your data. To select an entire column, use ⌘ + ⇧ + Down Arrow. If you need to hide sensitive data for a client view, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 0 for columns or ⌘ + ⌥ + 9 for rows.
Managing campaign data with filters and views

Media buyers often deal with messy exports. Before you start analyzing, create a filter. Select your header row and go to Data > Create a filter. This lets you sort by CPA or ROAS instantly. If you have too many columns, use View > Freeze to lock your campaign name and date columns. This keeps your labels visible while you scroll through performance metrics.

blocks.text: Google Sheets now supports up to 20 million cells. Even so, performance can drop if you have too many complex formulas. Avoid using too many VLOOKUP functions across different tabs. Instead, use IMPORTRANGE sparingly or keep your data in one sheet. If your sheet feels slow, remove unused rows at the bottom and unused columns on the right.
Common mistakes media buyers make in Sheets

The most common error is broken references. This happens when you delete a row that a formula relies on. Always use absolute references like $A$1 when you want a formula to stay fixed. Another common mistake is having multiple Google accounts active. This causes permission errors when you try to share a sheet. Use a dedicated Chrome profile for your work accounts to keep cookies and permissions separate.

When you are ready to send a report, do not just share the live link. Use File > Download > PDF document to create a static version. If you need to share access, use File > Share and set the access to Viewer. This prevents accidental edits to your master data. Always check the revision history by clicking the cloud icon if you suspect someone changed your formulas.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google Sheets is a web-based application. You can create a Progressive Web App shortcut in Chrome to give it a dedicated window and Dock icon.

faq.question: How do I speed up a slow spreadsheet?
faq.answer: Reduce the number of complex formulas, delete unused rows and columns, and avoid referencing data from too many external files.
